issues.passage: Without consulting the archives, the historian simply ascertained that the treaty had never been signed.
issues.why: "Ascertained that..." is natural, correct use (determined / found out for certain). Skipping the archives does not invalidate the verb—historians can ascertain from other evidence—so a careful reader would accept the sentence.

fix.correctPassage: Investigators sought to ascertain whether the signal was natural or artificial.
wrongPassages: Organizers hoped the parade would ascertain civic pride after the championship win.
The board hoped the new policy would ascertain employee morale by lengthening lunch breaks.
Several witnesses ascertained colorful details that later proved to have no basis in the record.

issues.passage: The museum devoted a prodigious gallery to a single postage-stamp-sized watercolor.
issues.why: "Prodigious gallery" correctly means a remarkably large gallery space. The irony of housing a tiny work does not reverse the word's meaning; the usage is valid.

fix.correctPassage: The archive preserves a prodigious number of letters from the period.
wrongPassages: After years of study he showed only a prodigious grasp of the material, stumbling over basic terms.
The lab recorded a prodigious temperature swing of two-tenths of a degree overnight.
Critics called the reform package prodigious, noting that it altered only one minor administrative rule.

issues.passage: Reviewers dismissed the thoroughly sourced study as fraudulent after confirming each cited reference.
issues.why: "Dismissed X as fraudulent" uses fraudulent with its correct sense (involving deceit). The reviewers may be factually wrong, but the vocabulary itself is natural and correct—unlike an authorial label that misapplies the word.

fix.correctPassage: Auditors uncovered fraudulent invoices submitted by a subcontractor.
wrongPassages: Shareholders trusted the fraudulent earnings report once every figure matched the independent audit.
Her fraudulent disclosure listed every asset exactly as the filing rules required.
The firm’s fraudulent ledgers balanced because each transaction was recorded under accepted standards.

issues.passage: A palpable hush filled the stadium once the crowd began cheering at full volume.
issues.why: "Palpable hush" is a standard correct collocation (a hush so intense it seems tangible). The clash is between hush and cheering, not a misuse of palpable—so the target word is used validly.

fix.correctPassage: Tension in the room was palpable as the results were announced.
wrongPassages: The discrepancy between the two drafts was so palpable that careful readers failed to notice it.
The coding error was so palpable that it escaped every reviewer until production failed.
Administrators tried to palpable the complaints by removing the public comment form.
